newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Skoda says made normal loan to boss.
newsitem.headline: Czech Skoda says made normal loan to boss.

text.p: Czech engineering concern Skoda a.s. on Tuesday said a separate company owned by its chief executive Lubomir Soudek received a 60 million crown loan from one of Skoda's subsidiaries.
But in a statement, the company denied a report in the daily Mlada Fronta Dnes that the credit was granted on interest-free terms.

Skoda said Soudek's investment firm NERo s.r.o. received the loan from one of Skoda's numerous subsidiaries, Skoda Jaderne Strojirenstvi (SJS) in 1994, but that NERo paid 15 percent interest on the credit.
Soudek's NERo took a 20 percent stake as part of the privatisation programme in 1993 for the Plzen-based conglomerate, one of the country's largest industrial groups.
Soudek has since been the company's chairman and chief executive.

A copy of a contract between NERo and SJS provided by Skoda shows that Soudek borrowed 60 million crowns in September 1994 with a repayment term of two-months and monthly interest charged at 1.25 percent, a rate of 15 percent per annum.
His firm provided shares worth a nominal 120 million crowns in the parent company Skoda a.s. as a guarantee.
Skoda a.s., no longer affiliated with the Czech auto maker now owned by Volkswagen AG, did not say for what purpose the loan was made, and officials were not immediately available to comment.
